items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: At this point, Jimmy Carter was the President. I was standing there playing this thing and thinking to myself how wonderful it might be if he can get some of his things going

ctx.x: Are there moments that you remember from your career of nights where you were playing where it was just – everything was right?

I have had a few of those. I’ve had a few nights like that and a few instances. I remember one time down in Sarasota. I was playing with John Bunch. We were playing Georgia. That’s a very nice piece of music. At the time, while I was playing it, I was thinking, when I was in the service in the South, there was so much racial friction, there was so much tension, and I kept saying to some of the fellows that I knew, and thinking of my own, that one day, if we had a Southern president, it might make a difference in…

about Jimmy Carter and about the political thing in this music, but that was exactly what I was thinking. It was unbelievable. It seemed like whatever I wanted to do, I did, and it just came off right. And there have been other times when I’ve had that good fortune.
